94.t: Eastern Han at its height · the Western Regions submit
94.d: In the Yongyuan era under Emperor He, Eastern Han territory reached its greatest extent. In 89 and 91 Dou Xian and Geng Kui twice routed the Northern Xiongnu, at Mount Jiluo and in the Jinwei Mountains; the Northern Chanyu fled west, the Xianbei seized the chance to move into the lands north of the Gobi, and more than 100,000 Xiongnu tents that stayed behind "all called themselves Xianbei". In 91 Ban Chao became Protector-General of the Western Regions, and in 94 he raised troops from eight states including Kucha and Shanshan to subdue Karasahr; the fifty-odd states of the Western Regions all sent hostages and submitted. The empire was divided into thirteen provinces and over a hundred commanderies and kingdoms, reaching the Yin Mountains and Liaodong in the north, Rinan in the south and the Pamirs in the west. In the same year more than 200,000 newly surrendered Southern Xiongnu rebelled and left the frontier.

184.d: In the 2nd month of Zhongping 1 under Emperor Ling, Zhang Jue, who had gathered several hundred thousand followers through the Way of Great Peace, rose in thirty-six divisions on the same day, his men wearing yellow turbans. Twenty-eight commanderies in seven provinces responded, most strongly Julu in Ji Province, Yingchuan and Runan in Yu Province, and Nanyang in Jing Province. The court lifted the Partisan Prohibitions and sent Huangfu Song, Zhu Jun and Lu Zhi against them: in the 5th month they burned out Bo Cai at Changshe; the siege of Zhang Mancheng's remnant at Wancheng lasted several months; in the 10th month Zhang Liang was crushed at Guangzong, and in the 11th month Zhang Bao was beheaded at Xiaquyang, ending the main rising. In winter the Huangzhong Auxiliary Hu rose in Liang Province with Beigong Boyu, Bian Zhang and Han Sui, and Song Jian of Fuhan styled himself "King of the River's Source who Pacifies Han".

189.d: In 188 Emperor Ling took Liu Yan's advice and turned the provincial Inspectors into Governors; Liu Yan went to Shu and Liu Yu took charge of You Province. In the 4th month of 189 Emperor Ling died, the Young Emperor came to the throne and Empress Dowager He held court. The General-in-Chief He Jin plotted with Yuan Shao to destroy the eunuchs and summoned Dong Zhuo and others to bring troops to the capital. In the 8th month He Jin was killed by Zhang Rang and the other eunuchs; Yuan Shao and Yuan Shu led troops into the palace and slaughtered the eunuchs, and in the chaos Dong Zhuo entered Luoyang, absorbed the forces of He Jin and Ding Yuan, and in the 9th month deposed the Young Emperor and set up Liu Xie, King of Chenliu, as Emperor Xian. Yuan Shao fled to Ji Province; Cao Cao went east under a false name and raised troops in Chenliu with his family's wealth. Gongsun Du in Liaodong, Han Sui and Ma Teng in Liang Province and Zhang Yan of the Black Mountain army in the Taihang each held a region of their own.

190.t: The eastern coalition against Dong Zhuo
190.d: In the 1st month the provinces and commanderies east of the passes rose together and chose Yuan Shao as leader of the alliance: Yuan Shao and Wang Kuang camped in Henei; Han Fu, Governor of Ji Province, stayed at Ye to supply grain; Kong Zhou, Inspector of Yu Province, camped in Yingchuan; Liu Dai, Zhang Miao, Qiao Mao, Yuan Yi, Bao Xin and Cao Cao camped at Suanzao; and Yuan Shu camped at Luyang in Nanyang. Dong Zhuo had the Young Emperor poisoned, and in the 2nd month burned the palaces of Luoyang and drove several million people west to Chang'an, staying in Luoyang himself to hold off the enemy. Fearing Dong Zhuo's strength, the allied armies feasted every day and dared not advance; only Cao Cao pursued west, and he was defeated on the Bian River at Xingyang. Sun Jian marched north from Changsha, killed Wang Rui, Inspector of Jing Province, and Zhang Zi, Administrator of Nanyang, and joined Yuan Shu. Liu Biao rode alone into Jing Province, and Gongsun Du set himself up independently in Liaodong.

191.t: Sun Jian enters Luoyang · Yuan Shao seizes Ji Province
191.d: After his defeat at Liangdong Sun Jian regrouped and advanced again, crushing Dong Zhuo's army at Yangren and beheading the commander Hua Xiong; in the 4th month he entered Luoyang and repaired the imperial tombs, while Dong Zhuo fell back to Chang'an. The coalition then turned on itself: in the 7th month Yuan Shao forced Han Fu to give up Ji Province and made himself Governor of Ji Province; Yuan Shu and Liu Biao fought over Jing Province, and Sun Jian, attacking Xiangyang, was ambushed and killed on Mount Xian (or 192). Cao Cao defeated Bai Rao of the Black Mountain army at Puyang, and Yuan Shao recommended him as Administrator of Dong Commandery. Gongsun Zan crushed the Qing Province Yellow Turbans at Dongguang and sent Tian Kai and Liu Bei into Qing Province against Yuan Shao. On Liu Yan's orders Zhang Lu seized Hanzhong and killed its Administrator Su Gu, then soon made himself independent.

192.t: Dong Zhuo killed · Cao Cao takes Yan Province
192.d: In spring Yuan Shao routed Gongsun Zan at Jieqiao (or the previous winter). In the 4th month the Minister over the Masses Wang Yun and Lü Bu killed Dong Zhuo, and the people of Chang'an sang and danced in the streets; in the 6th month Dong Zhuo's old officers Li Jue and Guo Si, following Jia Xu's plan, counterattacked Chang'an; Wang Yun was killed and Lü Bu fled. A million Qing Province Yellow Turbans entered Yan Province and killed the Inspector Liu Dai, and Bao Xin and others invited Cao Cao, Administrator of Dong Commandery, to become Governor of Yan Province. In winter Cao Cao pursued them to Jibei and took the surrender of more than 300,000 fighters and over a million men and women, choosing the best of them as the "Qing Province troops". Li Jue gave Ma Teng and Han Sui general's titles, and Liang Province nominally returned to the court.

193.d: In spring Yuan Shu marched north into Chenliu; Cao Cao crushed him at Kuangting, and Yuan Shu fled to Jiujiang, took Shouchun and made himself master of Yang Province. In autumn, citing the murder of his father Cao Song, Cao Cao attacked Tao Qian, Governor of Xu Province, took more than ten cities and routed the Xu Province army at Pengcheng, slaughtering widely as he went, so that "the Si River ceased to flow". Yuan Shao besieged the Black Mountain army at Mount Luchang in Wei Commandery. In winter Gongsun Zan attacked and killed Liu Yu, Governor of You Province, and took all of You Province. Ou Lian of Xianglin County in Rinan Commandery had killed the county magistrate the year before and set himself up as king; this was the beginning of the kingdom of Linyi.

194.d: In summer Cao Cao attacked Tao Qian again and overran Langya and Donghai; Liu Bei brought troops to relieve Tao Qian and camped east of Tan. While Cao Cao was away in the east, Zhang Miao and Chen Gong invited Lü Bu into Yan Province, and its commanderies and counties all went over to him except three cities, Juancheng, Fan and Dong'e, held by Xun Yu and Cheng Yu. Cao Cao turned back and faced Lü Bu at Puyang for more than a hundred days, until a locust plague and famine made both sides withdraw. In winter Tao Qian died of illness and Xu Province passed to Liu Bei. Liu Yan, Governor of Yi Province, died and was succeeded by his son Liu Zhang. Liu Yao, Inspector of Yang Province, crossed the Yangtze to govern from Qu'e and drove out Wu Jing, Yuan Shu's Administrator of Danyang, and Sun Ben; Sun Ce went to join Yuan Shu and attacked Lujiang for him.

195.t: Emperor Xian's return east · Sun Ce crosses the Yangtze
195.d: Cao Cao defeated Lü Bu again and again at Dingtao and Juye; Lü Bu fled east to Liu Bei and camped at Xiaopei. Cao Cao besieged Yongqiu, which fell in the 12th month; Zhang Chao killed himself and Yan Province was secured once more. Sun Ce borrowed a thousand-odd men from Yuan Shu and marched east, gathering five or six thousand by the time he reached Liyang; he crossed the Yangtze and routed Liu Yao at Niuzhu and Qu'e; Liu Yao withdrew to Yuzhang, and within a few months Sun Ce had tens of thousands of followers. In Chang'an Li Jue and Guo Si turned on each other; in the 7th month Emperor Xian left Chang'an for the east under the protection of Yang Feng, Dong Cheng and others, was badly defeated at Caoyang in Hongnong in the 12th month, and crossed the Yellow River by night to Anyi in Hedong. Yuan Shao's general Qu Yi joined Liu Yu's former officers Xianyu Fu and Yan Rou to rout Gongsun Zan at Baoqiu, and Gongsun Zan fell back to hold Yijing.

196.d: In the 7th month Emperor Xian returned to Luoyang, now in ruins; in the 8th month Cao Cao arrived and soon moved the emperor to Xu, "serving the Son of Heaven to command those who do not submit". In the same year, on the advice of Zao Zhi and Han Hao, he set up military farms around Xu that yielded a million hu of grain. While Liu Bei faced Yuan Shu at Xuyi and Huaiyin, Lü Bu seized Xiapi behind his back; Liu Bei went back to camp at Xiaopei and later, pressed by Lü Bu, went over to Cao Cao. Sun Ce defeated Wang Lang, Administrator of Kuaiji, and held all three commanderies of Wu, Kuaiji and Danyang. Yuan Tan defeated Kong Rong at Beihai, and all of Qing Province passed to the Yuans. Zhang Ji was killed by a stray arrow while attacking Rang, and his nephew Zhang Xiu took over his troops and camped at Wan.

197.d: In spring Yuan Shu proclaimed himself emperor at Shouchun with the dynastic name Zhong; Sun Ce broke with him, and Lü Bu beheaded his envoys. In the 1st month Cao Cao marched south against Zhang Xiu, who surrendered and then rebelled again; Cao Ang and Dian Wei were killed and Cao Cao was hit by a stray arrow. Yuan Shu sent assassins to kill Liu Chong, King of Chen; in the 9th month Cao Cao marched east, Yuan Shu abandoned his army and fled across the Huai, and Qiao Rui and the others he left behind were beheaded at Qiyang. Cao Cao recommended Sun Ce as Chief Commandant of Cavalry and heir to the title Marquis of Wucheng; the next year Sun Ce was made General Who Attacks Rebels and Marquis of Wu. Hua Xin, Administrator of Yuzhang, held his commandery after Liu Yao's death.

198.d: In the 3rd month Cao Cao attacked Zhang Xiu at Rang again but turned back on hearing that Yuan Shao meant to strike at Xu; Zhang Xiu pursued him and was beaten. In the 4th month Li Jue was killed, and Guanzhong was divided among Ma Teng, Han Sui, Duan Wei and other generals. In the 9th month Lü Bu sent Gao Shun to take Xiaopei and Liu Bei fled to Cao Cao; in the 10th month Cao Cao marched east and besieged Lü Bu at Xiapi, flooding the city with the Yi and Si rivers on the advice of Xun You and Guo Jia. In the 12th month Lü Bu's officers Song Xian and Wei Xu seized Chen Gong and surrendered; Lü Bu was strangled at the White Gate Tower, Zang Ba and others submitted, and Xu Province was pacified. Yuan Shao besieged Gongsun Zan at Yijing. Zhang Yang, who wanted to rescue Lü Bu, was killed by one of his own officers.

199.d: In the 3rd month Yuan Shao tunnelled into Yijing and Gongsun Zan burned himself to death. Yuan Shao now held all four provinces of Ji, Qing, You and Bing, and picked 100,000 elite troops and 10,000 horses to march south on Xu. In the 4th month Cao Cao destroyed Sui Gu at Shequan and took Henei, then advanced to Liyang and set up his defences at Guandu. In the 6th month Yuan Shu, abandoned by his followers and unable to reach Yuan Shao in the north, coughed blood and died at Jiangting. In the 11th month Zhang Xiu, on Jia Xu's advice, surrendered to Cao Cao with all his men. Liu Bei, sent to intercept Yuan Shu, used the chance to seize Xu Province, killing the Inspector Che Zhou and holding Xiapi and Xiaopei, and turned against Cao Cao again. Sun Ce struck west at Wancheng, defeated Liu Xun and took over the remnants of Yuan Shu's army, then crushed Huang Zu at Shayi; Hua Xin, Administrator of Yuzhang, surrendered his commandery.

200.d: In the 1st month the plot of the Edict in the Girdle was discovered and the General of Chariots and Cavalry Dong Cheng and others were killed. Cao Cao marched in person against Liu Bei, who fled to Yuan Shao; Guan Yu was captured and went over to Cao Cao. In the 2nd month Yuan Shao sent Yan Liang to besiege Baima; in the 4th month Cao Cao lifted the siege with a feint and a surprise strike, Guan Yu killed Yan Liang, and Wen Chou was lured into a trap and killed at Yanjin. The two armies faced each other at Guandu for months and Cao Cao's food ran out; in the 10th month Yuan Shao's adviser Xu You defected, and Cao Cao led 5,000 foot and horse in a night raid on Wuchao that burned Yuan Shao's grain. Zhang He and Gao Lan surrendered, the Yuan army collapsed, and Yuan Shao crossed back north of the Yellow River with only 800 horsemen. In the 4th month Sun Ce was attacked by assassins at Dantu and died; the nineteen-year-old Sun Quan succeeded him in Jiangdong.

204.d: In 201 Cao Cao defeated Yuan Shao again at Cangting, then turned back to drive Liu Bei out of Runan; Liu Bei went to Liu Biao in Jing Province and camped at Xinye. In the 5th month of 202 Yuan Shao died of illness and his youngest son Yuan Shang succeeded him; the eldest, Yuan Tan, refused to accept it and the brothers fought each other. In the 2nd month of 204, while Yuan Shang was attacking Yuan Tan, Cao Cao besieged Ye and flooded it with the Zhang River; in the 8th month Ye fell and Shen Pei was killed. Cao Cao made himself Governor of Ji Province and from then on made Ye his base. Yuan Shang fled north to Zhongshan and then went to his brother Yuan Xi, Inspector of You Province; Yuan Tan held Bohai and Pingyuan, surrendering and then rebelling. Gao Gan, Inspector of Bing Province, surrendered his province. At about this time Gongsun Kang split off the southern part of Lelang to form Daifang Commandery.

207.d: In the 1st month of 205 Cao Cao beheaded Yuan Tan at Nanpi, securing Ji and Qing provinces, and Zhang Yan of the Black Mountain army surrendered with more than 100,000 followers. In winter 205 Gao Gan rebelled again; in 206 Cao Cao broke through at Hu Pass, and Gao Gan was killed fleeing south to Jing Province. Yuan Shang and Yuan Xi fled to Tadun of the Liaoxi Wuhuan. In 207, following the plans of Guo Jia and Tian Chou, Cao Cao went out through Lulong Fort, cutting through mountains and filling valleys for more than 500 li, and in the 8th month crushed the Wuhuan at White Wolf Mountain, beheading Tadun and taking the surrender of over 200,000 people. In the 9th month Yuan Shang and Yuan Xi fled to Liaodong, where Gongsun Kang beheaded them and sent their heads to Cao Cao. The north was essentially unified. In the same year Liu Bei called on Zhuge Liang three times at Longzhong. Zhang Jin, Inspector of Jiao Province, who had fought Liu Biao for years, had been killed by his officer Ou Jing at about this time or earlier; Liu Biao sent Lai Gong to replace him as Inspector and Wu Ju as Administrator of Cangwu, while the court made Shi Xie General of the Household Who Pacifies the South, with oversight of the seven commanderies of Jiao Province.

208.d: In spring Sun Quan marched west against Jiangxia and beheaded Huang Zu. In the 1st month Cao Cao dug the Xuanwu Pool at Ye to train a navy; in the 6th month he abolished the Three Excellencies and made himself Chancellor, and in the 7th month he marched south. In the 8th month Liu Biao died of illness, and in the 9th month Liu Cong surrendered the province. Liu Bei retreated south and was caught by Cao Cao's light cavalry at Changban near Dangyang; with Zhuge Liang, Zhang Fei, Zhao Yun and a few dozen horsemen he escaped to Hanjin, joined Guan Yu's fleet and Liu Qi of Jiangxia, and fell back to hold Xiakou. Zhuge Liang went to Chaisang to persuade Sun Quan, and Zhou Yu and Lu Su argued hard for resisting Cao Cao. In winter Zhou Yu and Cheng Pu brought 30,000 Wu troops to join Liu Bei and met Cao Cao's army at Red Cliffs; Huang Gai feigned surrender and attacked with fire, and Cao Cao's army was routed. Cao Cao withdrew north along the Huarong Road, leaving Cao Ren to hold Jiangling and Yue Jin to hold Xiangyang. In the 12th month Sun Quan besieged Hefei without success.

210.t: Zhou Yu takes Jiangling · the loan of Jing Province
210.d: After Red Cliffs Zhou Yu besieged Jiangling for a year; at the end of 209 Cao Ren abandoned the city and withdrew north, and Zhou Yu became Administrator of Nan Commandery. Liu Bei recommended Liu Qi as Inspector of Jing Province and marched south against the four commanderies of Wuling, Changsha, Guiyang and Lingling, taking all the land south of the Yangtze; after Liu Qi died of illness, Liu Bei made himself Governor of Jing Province with his seat at Gong'an, and Sun Quan gave him his sister in marriage. At one point Liu Bei went in person to Jingkou to see Sun Quan and asked to be given command of Jing Province. In 210 Zhou Yu died at Baqiu; Lu Su took over his troops, argued strongly for the alliance with Liu Bei, and urged Sun Quan to lend Nan Commandery to Liu Bei so that they could resist Cao Cao together. Bu Zhi became Inspector of Jiao Province, and Shi Xie and his brothers submitted to Sun Quan. At Ye Cao Cao issued his Edict Seeking the Worthy, calling for men "chosen for talent alone", and in winter built the Bronze Sparrow Terrace.

211.d: In the 3rd month Cao Cao sent Zhong Yao and Xiahou Yuan west on the pretext of attacking Zhang Lu. Ma Chao, Han Sui, Yang Qiu, Cheng Yi and the rest of the ten Guanzhong bands, suspicious and afraid, rose together and camped at Tong Pass. In the 7th month Cao Cao took the field in person, held them in front, and secretly sent Xu Huang and Zhu Ling across Puban Ford by night to camp west of the Yellow River; his main army then crossed north from Tong Pass and crossed the Wei southward from its north bank. In the 9th month he used Jia Xu's plan to sow distrust between Ma Chao and Han Sui and routed the coalition at Weinan; Ma Chao and Han Sui fled back to Liang Province and Guanzhong was pacified. Liu Zhang, afraid that Zhang Lu would attack him, took the advice of Zhang Song and Fa Zheng and invited Liu Bei into Shu; Liu Bei led his army to Fu to meet Liu Zhang. Sun Quan moved his seat from Jingkou to Moling, and the next year built Stone City and renamed the place Jianye.

214.d: In 212 Liu Bei turned back from Jiameng and attacked Liu Zhang to the south; in 213 he besieged Luocheng, where Pang Tong was killed by a stray arrow. Zhuge Liang, Zhang Fei and Zhao Yun came up the Yangtze into Shu to support him, and in summer 214 they besieged Chengdu; Ma Chao came over to Liu Bei, Liu Zhang surrendered, and Liu Bei became Governor of Yi Province. In 213 Cao Cao was raised to Duke of Wei, with ten commanderies of Ji Province forming the state of Wei and Ye as its capital. In the 1st month of the same year he attacked Ruxu; seeing the good order of Sun Quan's ships and arms, he sighed "A son should be like Sun Zhongmou" and withdrew. Fearing that Sun Quan would raid the commanderies along the Yangtze, he ordered their people to move inland, but more than 100,000 households in Lujiang, Jiujiang, Qichun and Guangling panicked and fled east across the river instead; "the land west of the river was emptied, and south of Hefei only Wancheng remained". From then on the land between the Yangtze and the Huai was abandoned land between the two states. In 213 Ma Chao attacked and killed Wei Kang, Inspector of Liang Province; the next year Yang Fu and Jiang Xu drove him out and he went to Zhang Lu. Xiahou Yuan pacified Longyou, and in the 10th month stormed and massacred Fuhan and beheaded Song Jian. In the 5th month of 214 Sun Quan marched in person on Wancheng, took it in the intercalary month that followed, and captured Zhu Guang, Cao Cao's Administrator of Lujiang.

215.t: Cao Cao takes Hanzhong · Xiaoyao Ford
215.d: Since Liu Bei now held Yi Province, Sun Quan sent envoys to demand the return of the Jing Province commanderies. Liu Bei refused and the two sides brought their armies to Yiyang, where Lu Su and Guan Yu met, "each with a single blade". Then, because Cao Cao was attacking Hanzhong, the two agreed on the Xiang River as their boundary: Changsha, Jiangxia and Guiyang in the east went to Sun Quan, and Nan Commandery, Lingling and Wuling in the west to Liu Bei. In the 7th month Cao Cao broke through Yangping Pass, and in the 11th month Zhang Lu surrendered; the peoples of Ba also submitted; Zhang He came south to Dangqu and was defeated by Zhang Fei. In the 8th month Sun Quan attacked Hefei with 100,000 men; Zhang Liao charged his lines with 800 men and pursued him at Xiaoyao Ford, nearly capturing him. In the 5th month Han Sui was killed by his own men and Liang Province was pacified.

219.t: Battle of Hanzhong · Battle of Xiangyang–Fancheng
219.d: In 216 Cao Cao was raised to King of Wei and divided the Southern Xiongnu into five divisions. In 217 Liu Bei advanced into Hanzhong and faced Xiahou Yuan at Yangping Pass. In the 1st month of 219 Huang Zhong beheaded Xiahou Yuan at Mount Dingjun; Cao Cao came in person but achieved nothing, and in the 5th month gave up Hanzhong (his "chicken rib" remark). In the 7th month Liu Bei proclaimed himself King of Hanzhong, and Meng Da and Liu Feng took Shangyong and Fangling. In the same month Guan Yu attacked Fancheng to the north; in the 8th month the Han River flooded, Yu Jin's seven armies were flooded out, Yu Jin surrendered and Pang De was beheaded, and the region south of Xu was shaken. Sun Quan secretly came to terms with Cao Cao, and in the intercalary 10th month Lü Meng crossed the river "in white" and took Jiangling and Gong'an. In the 12th month Guan Yu fled to Maicheng and was captured and killed at Linju. Lu Xun occupied Yiling and Zigui, and all of Jing Province passed to Sun Quan.

220.d: In the 1st month Cao Cao died at Luoyang and his son Cao Pi succeeded him as King of Wei and Chancellor. In the 7th month the Shu general Meng Da went over to Wei with Shangyong, Fangling and Xicheng, which Cao Pi combined into Xincheng Commandery. In the 10th month Emperor Xian of Han abdicated; Cao Pi took the throne on the Abdication Terrace at Fanyang in Yingchuan, changed the era to Huangchu and named his state Wei, and in the 12th month made Luoyang his capital. The Eastern Han came to an end after twelve emperors and 196 years. A rising by local strongmen in the Hexi commanderies of Liang Province was put down by Zhang Ji and Su Ze. On Chen Qun's proposal Wei adopted the nine-rank system. Sun Quan stayed at Gong'an and kept on good terms with Wei.

222.d: In the 4th month of 221 Liu Bei proclaimed himself emperor at Chengdu with the dynastic name Han, known to history as Shu Han; Zhang Fei was killed by his own officers. Sun Quan moved his capital to E County, renamed it Wuchang, and in the 8th month accepted the title King of Wu from Wei. In the 7th month Liu Bei marched in person against Sun Quan; in 222 his camps stretched for several hundred li to Xiaoting. Lu Xun held his ground and refused battle, and in the intercalary 6th month, in the summer heat and with the wind behind him, attacked with fire and destroyed more than forty Shu camps; Liu Bei fled by night to Yong'an (Baidi City). In the 9th month Sun Quan broke with Wei and changed his era to Huangwu; Wei sent Cao Xiu, Cao Zhen and Cao Ren against Wu in three columns, and the armies faced each other at Dongkou, Jiangling and Ruxu. Shanshan, Kucha and Khotan in the Western Regions sent envoys to Wei, and Wei re-established the Chief Clerk of the Western Regions.

225.d: In 223 Liu Bei died at Yong'an, entrusting his heir to Zhuge Liang, and Liu Shan came to the throne. Yong Kai, of a great family of Yizhou Commandery, killed the Administrator and went over to Wu; Gao Ding, a tribal king of Yuexi, and Zhu Bao, Assistant of Zangke Commandery, joined him, and Nanzhong rose in revolt. Zhuge Liang sent Deng Zhi to Wu and the Wu–Shu alliance was restored. In spring 225 Zhuge Liang led a large army south in person, entered Yuexi and beheaded Gao Ding; Yong Kai was killed by his own men and Meng Huo took over his followers. Holding that "winning hearts comes first" (by tradition he captured Meng Huo seven times and released him seven times), Zhuge Liang pacified Nanzhong by autumn. He renamed Yizhou Commandery as Jianning, created the new commanderies of Yunnan and Xinggu, and took the region's gold, silver, cinnabar, lacquer, plough oxen and warhorses for the state and army. In the 10th month Cao Pi led a fleet to Guangling, saw the surging waves of the Yangtze, sighed that Heaven had set it there to divide north from south, and turned back.

228.d: In 226 Cao Pi died and Cao Rui came to the throne. In the same year Shi Xie died; Sun Quan split his territory into Guang and Jiao provinces, Shi Xie's son Shi Hui refused to obey, and Lü Dai attacked and beheaded him; and Jiao Province came under Sun Wu's direct rule. In 227 Zhuge Liang submitted his Memorial on Dispatching the Troops and moved into Hanzhong. Meng Da, Administrator of Xincheng, plotted to go over to Shu; Sima Yi made a forced march of eight days to Shangyong and beheaded Meng Da in the 1st month of 228. In spring Zhuge Liang announced that he would take Mei by the Xie Valley and sent Zhao Yun and Deng Zhi as a decoy to hold Jigu, while he led the main army out by Mount Qi; the three commanderies of Tianshui, Nan'an and Anding went over to him. But Ma Su disobeyed orders, left the water supply to camp on a hill, and was routed by Zhang He at Jieting; Zhuge Liang moved over a thousand households from Xi County, took Jiang Wei with him and returned to Hanzhong. In the 8th month Zhou Fang, the Wu Administrator of Poyang, feigned surrender to lure the Wei Grand Marshal Cao Xiu into advancing deep, and Lu Xun routed him at Shiting. In the 12th month Zhuge Liang came out again through San Pass and besieged Chencang; Hao Zhao held out for over twenty days, and Zhuge Liang withdrew when his food ran out.

229.t: Sun Quan proclaims himself emperor · the Three Kingdoms established
229.d: In spring Zhuge Liang sent Chen Shi to take the two commanderies of Wudu and Yinping; Guo Huai came to their relief, and Zhuge Liang advanced to Jianwei and forced him back. In the 4th month Sun Quan took the imperial throne at Wuchang and changed the era to Huanglong; in the 9th month he moved his capital to Jianye, leaving Lu Xun to help the heir Sun Deng hold Wuchang. Shu Han sent Chen Zhen to Wu with congratulations, and the two states made a treaty agreeing to divide the realm between them once Wei was destroyed: Yu, Qing, Xu and You provinces would go to Wu, Yan, Ji, Bing and Liang provinces to Shu, with Si Province divided at Hangu Pass. With Wei, Shu and Wu each now under its own emperor, the three-way balance of power was formally established.

234.d: In 230 Cao Zhen and others attacked Shu by several routes but gave up after more than thirty days of heavy rain; in the same year Sun Quan sent Wei Wen and Zhuge Zhi with 10,000 armoured troops across the sea to Yizhou (today's Taiwan). In 231, on his fourth northern campaign, Zhuge Liang brought up grain with "wooden oxen" and besieged Mount Qi, harvested the wheat at Shanggui, and withdrew when Li Yan failed to keep up the grain supply, shooting down the pursuing Zhang He on the Mumen Road. In the 2nd month of 234 he led 100,000 men out through the Xie Valley, camped at the Wuzhang Plains, set some troops to farming, and faced Sima Yi across the Wei River for more than a hundred days. Sun Quan, as agreed, attacked Wei along three routes and besieged Hefei New City in person, but withdrew when Emperor Ming of Wei marched east. In the 8th month Zhuge Liang died of illness in camp; Yang Yi led the army home, Wei Yan was killed, and Jiang Wan took charge of the state.

238.d: In 233 Gongsun Yuan beheaded the envoys Sun Quan had sent to make him King of Yan and sent their heads to Wei. In 237 Guanqiu Jian, the Wei Inspector of You Province, was ordered to summon Gongsun Yuan, but was halted by rain at Liaosui and beaten back; Gongsun Yuan then made himself King of Yan and adopted the era name Shaohan. In the 1st month of 238 Sima Yi set out with 40,000 foot and horse and reached Liaodong in the 6th month; feinting at Liaosui, he made straight for Xiangping and encircled it after more than thirty days of heavy rain. The city fell in the 8th month; Gongsun Yuan and his son were beheaded, more than 7,000 men in the city aged fifteen or over were massacred, and the four commanderies of Liaodong, Daifang, Lelang and Xuantu passed to Wei. In this year Shu changed its era to Yanxi and Wu to Chiwu.

249.d: In 239 Emperor Ming of Wei died and the eight-year-old Cao Fang came to the throne, with Cao Shuang and Sima Yi as joint regents; Cao Shuang soon honoured Sima Yi as Grand Tutor to strip him of power. In the same year (or 238) Himiko, queen of Wa, sent envoys by way of Daifang Commandery to Luoyang and was given the title "King of Wa, Friend of Wei". In 241 a four-pronged Wu offensive northward achieved nothing. In 244 Cao Shuang attacked Shu through the Luo Valley with over 100,000 men, was stopped at Xingshi by Wang Ping and Fei Yi, and fell back in disarray; Guanqiu Jian campaigned east against Goguryeo and took Hwando. In the 1st month of 249, while Cao Shuang and his brothers accompanied the young emperor to pay respects at Emperor Ming's Gaoping Tomb, Sima Yi, long claiming to be ill, staged a coup in Luoyang. He persuaded Cao Shuang to surrender with the promise of "dismissal, not death", and a few days later had Cao Shuang, He Yan and others executed for treason and the three branches of their families wiped out. From then on power in Wei lay with the Sima family; Xiahou Ba fled to Shu. In autumn Jiang Wei came out into Longxi and built forts at Qucheng, and was defeated by Guo Huai and Chen Tai.

253.d: In 251 the Grand Commandant Wang Ling plotted at Shouchun to depose Cao Fang and set up Cao Biao, King of Chu; Sima Yi marched south in person and Wang Ling killed himself. This was the first of the Three Rebellions in Huainan. Sima Yi died the same year and his son Sima Shi took over the government. In 252 Sun Quan died and Sun Liang came to the throne with Zhuge Ke as regent. In winter Wei attacked Wu along three routes; Zhuge Ke routed Hu Zun and Zhuge Dan at Dongxing, where Ding Feng's men threw off their armour in the snow and charged with short weapons, and tens of thousands of Wei troops drowned scrambling over the pontoon bridge. In 253 Zhuge Ke threw the whole strength of the state, 200,000 men, against Hefei New City; Zhang Te held it for more than ninety days, plague broke out in the Wu army and more than half were killed or disabled, and after withdrawing Zhuge Ke was killed by Sun Jun. Fei Yi, Shu's General-in-Chief, was assassinated by a Wei defector, and Jiang Wei began to direct the northern campaigns.

258.t: The Three Rebellions in Huainan crushed
258.d: In 254 Sima Shi deposed Cao Fang and set up Cao Mao. In the 1st month of 255 Guanqiu Jian, General Who Guards the East, and Wen Qin, Inspector of Yang Province, rose at Shouchun (the second of the Three Rebellions in Huainan); Sima Shi took the field in person despite an eye ailment, crushed them in one campaign at Lejia and Xiang County, and died of illness soon after; his brother Sima Zhao succeeded him. In the same year Jiang Wei routed Wang Jing, Inspector of Yong Province, at Taoxi, but in 256 he was defeated by Deng Ai at Duangu. In 257 Zhuge Dan, General-in-Chief Who Attacks the East, rebelled at Shouchun with more than 100,000 men (the third of the Three Rebellions in Huainan), and Wu sent 30,000 men under Quan Yi, Wen Qin and others to help him. Sima Zhao took the emperor with him on campaign and besieged the city for nearly a year; it fell in the 2nd month of 258, Zhuge Dan was beheaded, and several hundred of his men submitted to execution with folded hands; not one surrendered. In Wu Sun Chen deposed Sun Liang and set up Sun Xiu, who promptly had Sun Chen executed. Tuoba Liwei of the Xianbei moved to Shengle in Dingxiang.

263.d: In 260 the Wei emperor Cao Mao led his palace servants against Sima Zhao and was stabbed to death by Cheng Ji, one of Jia Chong's men; Sima Zhao set up Cao Huan instead. In 263 Sima Zhao sent 180,000 men against Shu in three columns. Zhong Hui came out through the Luo and Xie valleys and took Yang'an Pass, and Jiang Wei fell back to hold Jiange against him. Deng Ai went from Yinping through more than 700 li of uninhabited country, cutting roads through the mountains and rolling down slopes wrapped in felt; in the 10th month he came out at Jiangyou, beheaded Zhuge Zhan and his son at Mianzhu, and in the 11th month closed on Chengdu. Liu Shan surrendered and Shu Han fell after two emperors and forty-three years. On imperial orders Jiang Wei surrendered to Zhong Hui at Fu. In the 5th month Lü Xing, an officer of Jiaozhi Commandery, killed Sun Xu, the Wu Administrator, and surrendered Jiaozhi to Wei; Jiuzhen and Rinan followed.

265.d: In the 1st month of 264 Zhong Hui and Jiang Wei plotted rebellion at Chengdu and were killed by mutinous troops; Deng Ai was also wrongly put to death. Sima Zhao was raised to King of Jin. In Wu Sun Xiu died, and the Chancellor Puyang Xing and others set up Sun Hao; Guang Province was split off from Jiao Province. In the 8th month of 265 Sima Zhao died and his son Sima Yan succeeded him; in the 12th month the Wei emperor Cao Huan abdicated, Sima Yan took the throne, named his state Jin, changed the era to Taishi and kept Luoyang as his capital, and Cao Wei came to an end. In the 9th month Sun Hao moved his capital to Wuchang, returning to Jianye the next year.

272.d: Jin put Yang Hu in command of Jing Province; he set up military farms and opened new land, and kept a peaceful border with the Wu general Lu Kang, the two exchanging envoys and courtesies. From 268 to 271 Wu sent Yu Si, Tao Huang, Xue Xu and others to recover Jiaozhi, Jiuzhen and Rinan. From 270 Tufa Shujineng of the Hexi Xianbei rebelled against Jin; Hu Lie, Inspector of Qin Province, was killed at Wanhudui, and Liang Province fell again and again. In the 8th month of 272 Bu Chan, the Wu commander at Xiling, surrendered his city to Jin. Jin sent Yang Zhao, Inspector of Jing Province, to relieve him, Yang Hu to attack Jiangling and Xu Yin, Army Supervisor of Badong, to strike at Jianping. Lu Kang built siege lines and held them while sending troops to meet each threat; in the 12th month he drove off Yang Zhao, took Xiling and beheaded Bu Chan. In the same year Emperor Wu of Jin secretly ordered Wang Jun, Inspector of Yi Province, to build a great fleet of tower ships at Chengdu.

280.d: In 279 Ma Long put down Tufa Shujineng. In winter Emperor Wu of Jin, following the plan left by Yang Hu (d. 278) and the advice of Du Yu and Zhang Hua, sent more than 200,000 men against Wu along six routes: Sima Zhou from Tuzhong, Wang Hun from west of the Yangtze, Wang Rong against Wuchang, Hu Fen against Xiakou, Du Yu against Jiangling, and Wang Jun and Tang Bin with the river fleet of Ba and Shu sailing downstream. In the 2nd month of 280 Wang Jun burned through the iron chains Wu had stretched across the Yangtze and took Xiling, Jingmen and Yidao in succession; Du Yu took Jiangling, and the lands south of the Yuan and Xiang rivers submitted as soon as they heard. In the 3rd month the Wu Chancellor Zhang Ti fell in battle at Banqiao, Wang Jun's tower ships sailed straight to Stone City, and Sun Hao surrendered with his hands bound; Wu was no more. The realm was reunited, and Jin gained Wu's four provinces, forty-three commanderies and 523,000 households.
